Tune them for resonance on the lowest frequency of operation
questions.explanation: All ground rods and earth connections should be bonded together with heavy-gauge wire or copper strap. This creates a single, unified ground system at equal potential, preventing dangerous voltage differences during lightning strikes.

questions.question: What hazard exists when rapidly charging or discharging an unprotected battery?
questions.explanation: Rapid charging or discharging generates excessive heat inside a battery and can cause electrolyte to vaporize or decompose (out-gassing), releasing flammable or toxic gases. In extreme cases, pressure buildup can cause the battery to rupture or explode.

questions.question: What hazard exists in a power supply immediately after turning it off?
answers: Circulating currents in the dc filter
Leakage flux in the power transformer
questions.explanation: Large filter capacitors in a power supply can retain dangerous voltages for seconds or minutes after the supply is turned off. Always wait for capacitors to discharge or use a bleeder resistor discharge path before working inside a power supply.

questions.question: Which of the following precautions should be taken when measuring high voltages with a voltmeter?
answers: Ensure that the voltmeter has very low impedance
Ensure that the voltmeter and its leads are rated for use at the voltages being measured
Ensure that the circuit is grounded through the voltmeter
Ensure that the voltmeter is set to the correct frequency
questions.explanation: High-voltage measurements require that both the meter and test leads be rated for the voltage being measured. Using under-rated leads can cause insulation breakdown, arcing, or electric shock.

questions.question: Which of the following is good practice when installing ground wires on a tower for lightning protection?
answers: Put a drip loop in the ground connection to prevent water damage to the ground system
Make sure all ground wire bends are right angles
Ensure that connections are short and direct
questions.explanation: Lightning protection ground conductors should be as short and straight as possible. Sharp bends and long runs add inductance that impedes lightning current flow and creates large voltage drops. Right-angle bends significantly increase inductance.

questions.question: What is required when climbing an antenna tower?
answers: Have sufficient training on safe tower climbing techniques
Use appropriate tie-off to the tower at all times
Always wear an approved climbing harness
questions.explanation: All three are required: training ensures you know safe techniques; a climbing harness is always required; and being tied off at all times means you're always secured even if you lose your grip. All three together are the minimum requirement.

questions.question: Under what circumstances is it safe to climb a tower without a helper or observer?
answers: When no electrical work is being performed
When no mechanical work is being performed
When the work being done is not more than 20 feet above the ground
questions.explanation: It is never safe to climb a tower alone. A helper or observer on the ground is always required to call for emergency assistance if the climber is injured or becomes incapacitated. No height or task type makes solo tower climbing acceptable.

questions.question: Which of the following is an important safety precaution to observe when putting up an antenna tower?
answers: Wear a ground strap connected to your wrist at all times
Insulate the base of the tower to avoid lightning strikes
Look for and stay clear of any overhead electrical wires
questions.explanation: The critical safety precaution when erecting a tower is identifying and staying well clear of overhead power lines. A tower or antenna contacting power lines can be instantly fatal. Tower bases are grounded, not insulated.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a safety wire through a turnbuckle used to tension guy lines?
answers: Secure the guy line if the turnbuckle breaks
Prevent loosening of the turnbuckle from vibration
Provide a ground path for lightning strikes
Provide an ability to measure for proper tensioning
questions.explanation: Turnbuckles used in guy lines can slowly unscrew due to wind vibration. Safety wire (or cotter pins) threaded through the turnbuckle prevents this rotation, maintaining proper guy wire tension indefinitely.

questions.question: What is the minimum safe distance from a power line to allow when installing an antenna?
answers: Add the height of the antenna to the height of the power line and multiply by a factor of 1.5
The height of the power line above ground
Enough so that if the antenna falls, no part of it can come within 10 feet of the power wires
questions.explanation: The antenna must be positioned far enough from power lines that if it completely collapses or falls, no part of it (including feed lines) can come within 10 feet of the power wires. This prevents electrocution from a structural failure.

questions.question: Which of the following is an important safety rule to remember when using a crank-up tower?
answers: This type of tower must never be painted
This type of tower must never be grounded
This type of tower must not be climbed unless it is retracted, or mechanical safety locking devices have been installed
questions.explanation: Crank-up (telescoping) towers must never be climbed while extended unless mechanical safety locks pin the sections in place. The sections can collapse under the climber's weight, resulting in fatal injuries.

questions.question: Which is a proper grounding method for a tower?
answers: A single four-foot ground rod, driven into the ground no more than 12 inches from the base
A ferrite-core RF choke connected between the tower and ground
A connection between the tower base and a cold-water pipe
Separate eight-foot ground rods for each tower leg, bonded to the tower and each other
questions.explanation: Proper tower grounding requires 8-foot ground rods driven at each tower leg, all bonded together and to the tower. Multiple deeper rods at each leg provide the lowest ground resistance for safely dissipating lightning energy.

questions.question: Why should you avoid attaching an antenna to a utility pole?
answers: The antenna will not work properly because of induced voltages
The antenna may unbalance the power transformer, causing power fluctuations
The antenna could contact high-voltage power lines
questions.explanation: Utility poles carry high-voltage power lines. Attaching an antenna to a utility pole risks contact between the antenna, feed line, or installer and those high-voltage lines, which can be instantly fatal. It is also typically illegal without utility permission.

questions.question: Which of the following is true when installing grounding conductors used for lightning protection?
answers: Wires must be carefully routed with precise right-angle bends
questions.explanation: Lightning protection conductors must be routed with gentle, sweeping curves — sharp bends create inductance that impedes lightning current and causes dangerous voltage spikes that can arc to nearby equipment. Short, straight runs with gentle curves are ideal.

questions.question: Which of the following establishes grounding requirements for an amateur radio tower or antenna?
questions.explanation: Grounding requirements for amateur radio towers and antenna installations are established by local electrical codes (based on the National Electrical Code, NEC). FCC Part 97 addresses radio operation, not electrical installation practices.

questions.question: What type of radiation are radio signals?
questions.explanation: Radio signals are non-ionizing radiation — they do not have enough energy per photon to remove electrons from atoms or break chemical bonds. Ionizing radiation (X-rays, gamma rays, alpha, beta particles) can damage DNA; RF cannot, though it can heat tissue.

questions.question: Which of the following bands has the lowest maximum permissible exposure for RF safety?
questions.explanation: The human body absorbs RF energy most efficiently in the 30–300 MHz range, with peak absorption around 50–100 MHz for an average adult. The FCC's MPE limits are most restrictive (lowest) at 50 MHz because absorption is highest there.

questions.question: How does the allowable power density for RF safety change if duty cycle changes from 100 percent to 50 percent?
answers: It increases by a factor of 3
It increases by a factor of 2
There is no adjustment allowed for lower duty cycle
questions.explanation: RF exposure limits are based on average power over a time period. If duty cycle drops from 100% to 50%, the average power is halved, allowing the peak power density to double (increase by a factor of 2) while maintaining the same average exposure.

questions.question: What factors affect the RF exposure of people near an amateur station antenna?
answers: Frequency and power level of the RF field
Distance from the antenna to a person
questions.explanation: All three factors determine RF exposure: frequency affects body absorption rate; power determines field strength; distance follows inverse square law (double distance = quarter power density); and radiation pattern determines direction of maximum exposure.

questions.question: Why do exposure limits vary with frequency?
answers: Lower frequency RF fields have more energy than higher frequency fields
Lower frequency RF fields do not penetrate the human body
Higher frequency RF fields are transient in nature
The human body absorbs more RF energy at some frequencies than at others
questions.explanation: The human body's RF energy absorption rate (SAR — Specific Absorption Rate) varies with frequency, with peak absorption in the 30–300 MHz range. The FCC's MPE limits are set to limit SAR, so limits must vary with the frequency-dependent absorption rate.

questions.question: Which of the following is an acceptable method to determine whether your station complies with FCC RF exposure regulations?
answers: By calculation based on FCC OET Bulletin 65
By calculation based on computer modeling
By measurement of field strength using calibrated equipment
questions.explanation: FCC RF exposure compliance can be demonstrated by any of these methods: manual calculations using OET Bulletin 65 formulas, computer modeling, or actual field strength measurements with calibrated equipment.

questions.question: What hazard is created by touching an antenna during a transmission?
questions.explanation: Touching a transmitting antenna causes RF burns — tissue damage from the heating effect of RF current flowing through skin. RF burns can occur even at low power levels, especially at frequencies where the body efficiently absorbs RF energy.

questions.question: Which of the following actions can reduce exposure to RF radiation?
questions.explanation: The most effective way to reduce RF exposure is to increase distance from the antenna — moving antennas farther from occupied areas. Relocating the transmitter (if not near the antenna) has minimal effect; increasing duty cycle increases exposure.

questions.question: How can you make sure your station stays in compliance with RF safety regulations?
answers: By informing the FCC of any changes made in your station
By re-evaluating the station whenever an item in the transmitter or antenna system is changed
By making sure your antennas have low SWR
By using only Underwriter Laboratories approved transmitting equipment
questions.explanation: FCC rules require re-evaluation of RF exposure whenever the station changes (power level, antenna type or location, operating frequency, etc.). Informing the FCC is not required; you just need to ensure continued compliance through re-evaluation.

questions.question: Why is duty cycle one of the factors used to determine safe RF radiation exposure levels?
answers: It affects the average exposure to radiation
It affects the peak exposure to radiation
It takes into account the antenna feed line loss
It takes into account the thermal effects of the final amplifier
questions.explanation: Biological effects of RF exposure are based on heating, which depends on average power absorbed over time. Duty cycle directly determines average power — a 50% duty cycle halves average exposure compared to continuous transmission at the same peak power.

questions.question: What is the definition of duty cycle during the averaging time for RF exposure?
answers: The difference between the lowest and highest power output of a transmitter
The difference between the PEP and the average power output of a transmitter
The percentage of time that a transmitter is transmitting
The percentage of time that a transmitter is not transmitting
questions.explanation: Duty cycle for RF exposure is the percentage of time the transmitter is actually transmitting during the averaging period (typically 6 minutes for controlled environments). A station transmitting 3 of every 6 minutes has 50% duty cycle.

questions.question: How does RF radiation differ from ionizing radiation (radioactivity)?
answers: RF radiation does not have sufficient energy to cause chemical changes in cells and damage DNA
RF radiation can only be detected with an RF dosimeter
RF radiation is limited in range to a few feet
questions.explanation: The key difference is photon energy. Ionizing radiation (X-rays, gamma rays) has enough energy per photon to ionize atoms and break DNA. RF photons have far less energy — they can only cause thermal (heating) effects, not ionization.

questions.question: Who is responsible for ensuring that no person is exposed to RF energy above the FCC exposure limits?
answers: Anyone who is near an antenna
questions.explanation: The station licensee bears full responsibility for ensuring their station's RF emissions do not expose any person (operators, bystanders, or neighbors) to levels exceeding the FCC's Maximum Permissible Exposure limits.
